note: Part B (drawing) is not transcribed: no model answer exists.

questions.text: How many times does the shape sequence (shown on the top) appear in the grid below? The sequence may appear top-to-bottom, bottom-to-top, left-to-right, right-to-left or at an angle.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The sequence is hexagon, circle, square, upright triangle. Start from each of the five hexagons in the grid and look in all eight directions for a circle next to it, then a square and a triangle in the same line. Four runs complete: down the second column from row 2, along row 3 from column 1, diagonally from the hexagon at the end of row 3 down to the left, and leftwards along the bottom row from the corner hexagon. The sideways (right-pointing) triangles are a different shape and are not counted.

questions.text: The bold lines correspond to four different paths P, Q, R and S. What is the length of the longest path? The length of each side of the square grids is 7 units. Use 22/7 as the value for \(\pi\).
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Trace each path from left to right and add its pieces: a straight cell side is 7, a quarter circle of radius one cell (or a half circle of radius half a cell) is 11, and a quarter circle of radius two cells (or a half circle of radius one cell) is 22. P = 7 + 11 + 7 + 22 + 11 + 11 + 14 + 11 + 11 + 22 = 127. Q = 11 + 22 + 11 + 21 + 11 + 11 + 22 + 11 = 120. R = 22 + 11 + 11 + 11 + 22 + 56 = 133. S = 11 + 7 + 22 + 22 + 14 + 22 + 11 + 22 = 131. The longest is R, 133 units.

questions.text: What is the maximum number of stars that can be packed inside the blue colour boundary including the one that is shown in the image below? The stars can be scaled but should not overlap. At least 4 points of every star should touch the blue colour boundary.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The two long blue edges meet at a point beyond the right end, so each next star is a smaller copy of the first, scaled towards that point. The next star's top point sits at the first star's upper right point, and its left point fits into the notch of the first star, so they touch without overlapping; each star is about 0.65 times the previous one. Measuring along the figure, the sixth star's right points land at the short right edge of the boundary and a seventh would not fit, so 6 stars fit.

questions.text: A dice throw can result in the numbers 2, 3, 5 or 6. Every 4th throw will result in 3. What is the minimum number of times the dice has to be thrown for the pawn to move from zero to reach exactly at 100?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The board has ladders only: 3 to 61, 6 to 75, 11 to 47, 23 to 37, 49 to 92, 63 to 83 and 82 to 99. No pair of throws reaches 94, 95, 97 or 98, so 3 throws cannot finish, and 4 throws would need 97 after three throws (the 4th throw is fixed at 3), which is also unreachable. Five throws work: 5 (to 5), 6 (to 11, ladder to 47), 2 (to 49, ladder to 92), the forced 3 (to 95), then 5 (to 100).

questions.text: Count the number of human figures in the picture.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Count region by region. Upper balcony, left part: 5 people (including one seen from the back behind a pillar); upper balcony, right part: 7. Foreground left: the woman, the person behind her and the man seen from the back, 3. One small figure behind the hanging lamp. The crowd in the central doorway: 6, including the man walking towards us. Right side: the woman on the stairs, the person behind the counter, the person bent over the counter, the woman with the bun and the old man, 5. Total 5 + 7 + 3 + 1 + 6 + 5 = 27.

questions.text: In the figure given below, the area of the largest regular hexagon is 720 units. What is the area of the shaded portion?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The dashed guide lines show the middle hexagon has half the side of the largest and the smallest has a quarter of its side. Area scales with the square of the side, so the smallest hexagon has area 720 divided by 16, which is 45. The small hexagon is drawn as a cube made of three equal rhombi, and two of them are shaded, so the shaded area is two thirds of 45, which is 30.

questions.text: A tetrahedron of side 18 units and a cone having base diameter of 10 units are cutting through a sphere as shown. Count the total number of surfaces in the resultant sphere.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Pushed right through along their axes, the tetrahedron cuts a triangular hole with 3 flat faces and the cone cuts a round hole of diameter 10. Both holes pass through the centre. The circle of diameter 10 fits inside the triangle of side 18 (its inscribed circle has diameter about 10.4), so the triangular hole cuts the round hole completely in two. Surfaces: the outer sphere 1, three flat faces 3, and two separate curved pieces of the round hole 2, a total of 6.

questions.text: Tim cycled from his house to his friend John's house and then on to his (Tim's) school without stopping. The average speed for his entire journey was 26 km/hr. The distance from John's house to Tim's school is 0.3 times the distance from Tim's house to John's house. Tim's speed from John's house to Tim's school was twice that of Tim's speed from Tim's house to John's house. What was Tim's average speed from John's house to Tim's school in km/hr?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Let the first leg be d at speed v, so the second leg is 0.3d at speed 2v. Total time is d/v + 0.3d/(2v) = 1.15d/v and total distance is 1.3d. Average speed 1.3v/1.15 = 26 gives v = 23 km/hr, so the speed from John's house to school is 2v = 46 km/hr.

questions.text: Identify the total number of differences in the images shown below.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Compare the two pictures part by part. Differences: the shape of the girl's hair bow, one book spine colour on the shelf, an extra pink crayon on the table, the pointing boy's tongue, the badge on the right girl's shirt, a button missing on the middle boy's shirt, the stripe on the girl's tie under her arm, the angle of the pencil on the floor, and the cherry on the cupcake. That makes 9.

questions.text: Count the number of cats in the given image.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: The picture is made of overlapping see-through cat silhouettes, each a sitting cat with two pointed ears and a curling tail. Count heads rather than bodies: find each pair of pointed ears with the notch between them, and tick each one off, working from the top of the cluster down. Where two silhouettes overlap, follow each outline separately so a shared edge is not counted twice. IIT Bombay's final key gives 11. This is a dense picture, so a careful count can easily land one off.

questions.text: Two trains of unequal length have speeds of 60 and 50 km/hr. When they travel in opposite directions in straight line tracks, they take 9 seconds to completely cross each other. When they travel in the same direction, a person in the faster train sees the slower train for 18 seconds. For how much time (in seconds) would a person in the slower train see the faster train when the trains travel in the same direction?
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: In opposite directions the relative speed is 110 km/hr, about 30.56 m/s, so the two lengths add to 30.56 times 9 = 275 m. In the same direction the relative speed is 10 km/hr = 25/9 m/s; the person in the faster train passes the slower train's length in 18 s, so the slower train is 50 m long and the faster train 225 m. A person in the slower train sees the faster train for 225 divided by 25/9 = 81 seconds.

questions.text: The image shows the profile of the blade which is designed to turn a wooden block, rotating about the axis PQ. Calculate the volume of the turned wooden block between P and Q. Consider the value of \(\pi\) to be 22/7.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The block left behind is the region between the blade edge and the axis, turned about PQ. From 0 to 4 the edge rises in a straight line from radius 0 to radius 1, giving a cone of volume one third of pi times 1 squared times 4, which is 4pi/3. From 4 to 6 the edge is a quarter circle of radius 2 centred on the axis at 4, giving a hemisphere of volume two thirds of pi times 8, which is 16pi/3. Total 20pi/3 = 440/21, about 20.95.

questions.text: A blue colour liquid is used completely to make a star shaped jelly using the mould shown on the right. What is the value of 'X' in cm? Ignore the wall thickness of the mould and consider the value of \(\pi\) to be 22/7.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: The liquid fills a cylinder of diameter 12 cm to a height of 6.6 cm, written as 3.8 times root 3, so its volume is (22/7) times 36 times 3.8 root 3. The six-pointed star with edge X is made of 12 small equilateral triangles of side X, so its area is 3 root 3 times X squared, and with depth 4 cm its volume is 12 root 3 times X squared. Equating, X squared = (22/7) times 3 times 3.8, about 35.8, so X is about 6 cm.

questions.text: What number replaces the question mark? (The paper prints only the picture for this question.)
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: Read the six sticks of each box as a 6-digit binary number, a red head being 1 and a plain stick 0. The first box is 001000 = 8, then 001010 = 10, 001011 = 11, 001101 = 13, 001110 = 14 and 010001 = 17. The last box is 010100, which is 16 + 4 = 20.

questions.text: Shown below are four sides of a rectangular dice. If 3 such dice are thrown together, what is the probability of getting a total sum of 4? Consider the value of the blank side to be zero.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each die shows 0, 1, 2 or 3 with equal chance, so three dice have 4 cubed = 64 outcomes. Ways to make 4 from three values each 0 to 3: all ways of splitting 4 into three parts is 15, minus the 3 ways that use a 4, leaving 12. The probability is 12/64 = 3/16 = 0.1875.

questions.text: How many distinct types of characters appear in the figure given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Many characters differ only in a small stroke: a straight tail, an arrow tail or a hooked tail at the bottom; a short tick, a tall stroke, a slash or a curled flag on top. Group the 49 characters by matching every stroke. The groups, with how often each occurs, are 5, 3, 3, 1, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4, 4, 1, 2, 1, 2, 1, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1, 1, 1, 1, which is 23 different characters adding to 49.

questions.text: Objects made out of cardboard are shown in the image below. Count the number of objects shown as open containers in this image.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.solution: Closed objects are the cubes with a white lid, the pyramids and the tall obelisks. Open containers show their inside walls: the dark cubes whose top shows two inner walls (9), the dark trays that widen upwards with their inner rim visible (6), and the sloped trays whose white floor and grey inner walls show (6). Total 9 + 6 + 6 = 21.

questions.text: A triangular pyramid with equal sides can be flipped on its edges without slipping or sliding as shown on the left. What is the minimum number of flips needed for the pyramid to reach the finishing line if the starting position is as shown on the right?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Seen from above, the pyramid's base is an equilateral triangle of side 30, height about 26, and each flip moves it to the neighbouring triangle across one edge. Moving up one row of triangles takes two flips: one over a slanted edge to the inverted triangle, then one over its top edge. The line is 135 away, which is in the sixth row (rows span 0 to 26, 26 to 52, and so on, the sixth from 129.9 to 155.9). Reaching the upright triangle in the sixth row takes 5 times 2 = 10 flips.

questions.text: Shown in the top row are 4 pieces of building blocks. Which of the option(s) is/are made using all four pieces?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: All four pieces have the same depth, so compare the end profiles: a right-angled half-square wedge, a square (the cube), a slanted parallelogram of the same width and height, and a second triangular wedge, a total of three square units. Two triangles placed together make a slanted parallelogram, and a cube on a standing parallelogram makes a block two units tall, which gives B. A ramp built from the wedges and the slanted block gives A, and placing the triangles at the two ends of the cube and the parallelogram gives the six-sided block C. D has a base slab much thinner than any piece, so it cannot be built.

questions.text: A printer wishes to print four colours, Crimson, Pink, Brown, and Indigo, using CMYK [Cyan, Magenta, Yellow and Key (black)] inks. The printer uses the CMYK combinations shown below (in % of each ink) to produce the colours on the right. Which combination(s) will result in the correct colour(s)?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Magenta and yellow together make red, so high magenta with a lot of yellow and little cyan (A) gives crimson. B has little magenta and a lot of yellow, which prints a pale yellow, not pink; pink needs high magenta and little yellow. C has equal cyan and magenta with full yellow, which gives a muddy olive brown rather than the reddish brown shown, which needs much more magenta than cyan. D mixes cyan and a lot of magenta with no yellow, which gives the purple shown.

questions.text: Which of the statement(s) is/are true?

options.label: A
options.text: Jharkhand has the highest number of sportspersons but its percentage of women representation is not the highest.

options.label: B
options.text: Of all the North-Eastern states, Nagaland produces the highest number of sportspersons.

options.label: C
options.text: Jammu & Kashmir has low number of sportspersons but high women's representation.

options.label: D
options.text: Even though Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh have the same number of sportspersons, Uttar Pradesh fares higher in women's representation as compared to Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Language
questions.solution: Jharkhand has the most sportspersons (759) but 50.1% women, below Nagaland's 73.5%, so A is true. Among the North-Eastern states Manipur has 358, far more than Nagaland's 34, so B is false. Jammu and Kashmir has few sportspersons (73) and also the lowest women's share (10.9%), so C is false. Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh both have 405, and Uttar Pradesh has 43.4% women against Tamil Nadu's 30.6%, so D is true.

questions.text: Shown on the left is a sheet of stickers. Identify the option(s) in which monkeys of the same species are sitting together.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: The sheet has two kinds of monkey: langurs (black faces, very long tails, such as the standing one whose tail loops over its head, the sitting one with a looped tail and the mother lying with a long curled tail) and macaques (the others, with shorter tails). Match each silhouette group to its stickers by the tails and poses. In A and C each group is either all langurs (the looped-tail standing langur with the other two langurs) or all macaques. In B and D the looped-tail langur shares a group with macaques such as the walking one.

questions.text: Different views of the cross section of a fish toy are shown here. The points P and Q are connected in such way that the fish tail waves. The grey colour gear and the green colour part are joined together. The rod is free to move depending on how it is connected to the green part. Which of the option(s) will work to wave the tail?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge

questions.text: A tourist is shooting photographs of an ancient building from four locations A, B, C and D marked by x. The tourist is using only one camera without changing its magnification. Identify the location(s) in the floor plan which will result in the given photograph.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: The photograph looks down a central aisle with five pillars on each side, the nearest pair just beside the camera at the edges of the frame. From A, looking up the middle, the two central columns each have five pillars, starting right in front of the camera. From D, looking left between the third and fourth rows, each row also has five pillars ahead, the sixth pillar being behind the camera. From C only four pillars lie ahead in each central column, and from B the two sides are unequal (two pillars in the top row against five in the next). So A and D give the photograph.

questions.text: The options show four ways of attempting to write the word "universe" in a mix of lower-case and upper-case letters. Which of the option(s) is/are correctly read as "universe"?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity

questions.text: Which of the option(s) is/are from the same font family (i.e. weight and/or width variations) of the words given below?
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity

questions.text: Which of the pieces could be used four times individually to form a square? The pieces can be rotated and flipped but should not be overlapped.
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each piece must have a quarter of the square's area. A is a trapezoid half the square wide whose two parallel sides add up to the square's side, so two of them (one turned upside down) make a half-square strip, and two strips make the square. B has a right angle at one corner and another right angle where its two equal cut edges meet, the shape you get by cutting a square through its centre with two perpendicular slanted lines, so four of them make a pinwheel square. D is a quarter square with a bulge on one side matching the scoop on the next side, so four interlock like jigsaw pieces. C's notch and its triangular tab are on different sides at different positions, so four copies cannot close up.

questions.text: Shown below is a coconut broken into two pieces. Identify the correct representation(s) of the coconut.
questions.subject: Observation and Design Sensitivity
questions.subtopic: Matching a part to the whole
questions.solution: A coconut has its three eyes at one end only, the end where the tuft of husk fibre is usually left on. So of the two halves, only one can show the eyes or the tuft, and the other half is plain. A shows a plain half and a half with the tuft (covering the eyes), and C shows a half with the eyes and a plain half, so both are possible. B puts the eyes on one half and the tuft on the other, and D puts eyes on both halves, which cannot happen.

questions.text: Shown below is an image of solid rings of black and white patterns. A ring going inside another is called a link. Which of the statement(s) is/are TRUE.

options.label: A
options.text: All rings are linked to form one continuous chain.

options.label: B
options.text: One ring does not have any link.

options.label: D
options.text: Two rings have only one link.

questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Each ring is drawn in black and white segments, and the white segments hide what is behind them, so at every crossing the ring that is in front cuts off the black of the ring behind. Two rings are linked when each is in front at one of their two crossings. Checking the crossings of the six rings in turn, they form a single chain, so the two end rings each have only one link.

questions.text: The options show different configurations of refill bottles of mosquito repellent, for an atypical socket shown on the left. After fitting, the red mark on the refill bottle must align with the red mark on the machine. Which of the option(s) will allow all of the liquid to be consumed?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: The socket is tilted 25 degrees, so the fitted bottle hangs tilted by 25 degrees. A has a flat bottom with the wick in the middle, so when tilted the last of the liquid runs to one corner away from the wick. B and C have cone-shaped bottoms sloping at 30 degrees towards the wick; a 25 degree tilt still leaves every part of the floor sloping down to the wick, so it soaks up all the liquid. In D the neck is set at 30 degrees, so on the tilted socket the body hangs almost upright, tipped slightly towards the corner where the wick ends, and the liquid collects there.

questions.subject: Environment and Society

questions.text: In which of the option(s) dust-bin lids will open?
questions.subject: Practical and Scientific Knowledge
questions.solution: Pressing the pedal turns the bottom lever about its pivot. In A, B and D the lever has one pivot, so its left end rises and pushes the rod up; in C the lever has an extra pivot and joint, which reverses it, so the rod is pulled down. The lid opens only if the rod pushes up on a point on the lid's side of the lid's hinge, or pulls down on a point on the far side. In B the rod pushes up just to the lid's side of the hinge, and in C the rod pulls down on the tab beyond the hinge, so both open. In A and D the rod pushes up on the tab beyond the hinge, which only presses the lid shut.

questions.text: On 16th July 2022, Parvathy bought 4 new pairs of socks A, B, C and D to train herself for the Marathon race on Gandhi Jayanti. She started her training next day wearing the new socks. She trained every day, including the day of the marathon, wearing the socks (one pair every day) in the following sequence: C, A, B and D. Unfortunately, she could not train from 3rd to 22nd September 2022 as she was unwell. She resumed her training on 23rd wearing pair 'A' socks and continued with the same sequence till the event day. Identify the pair of socks that Parvathy wore the maximum during her entire training period.
questions.subject: Analytical and Logical Reasoning
questions.solution: From 17 July to 2 September is 15 + 31 + 2 = 48 days, exactly 12 rounds of C, A, B, D, so each pair is worn 12 times. From 23 September to 2 October (Gandhi Jayanti) is 10 days starting with A: A, B, D, C, A, B, D, C, A, B, so A and B get 3 more and C and D 2 more. Totals: A 15, B 15, C 14, D 14, so A and B are worn the most.

questions.text: The rectilinear hollow box shown on the left is cut along plane 1 and plane 2. Which of the option(s) show(s) correct unfolded pieces?
questions.subject: Visualization and Spatial Reasoning
questions.solution: Plane 1 is the upright plane through the top face's diagonal and plane 2 runs straight back through the front face's diagonal, so the hollow box falls into four pieces. Two pieces are a side face (a rectangle) with a triangle from the front or back face and a triangle from the top or bottom face; both triangles have their right angle at the same corner of the rectangle, as in B, but not A, where they are at different corners. The other two pieces are just two triangles joined along a box edge, a large one (width by height) and a small one (width by depth), with their right angles at opposite ends of the shared edge, as in C; D has both right angles at the same end.
